stories.title: Phillies Force Wild Card Game 3 With Dramatic Extra-Inning Comeback
stories.angle: Philadelphia Phillies rallied from behind to beat the Atlanta Braves 4-3 in 10 innings in Game 2 of the NL Wild Card Series on September 30. Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper hit back-to-back home runs off Braves reliever Dylan Lee in the 8th to tie it. Alec Bohm delivered a walk-off homer off Didier Fuentes in the 10th. Series tied 1-1. Winner-take-all Game 3 is tonight (October 1) at Truist Park — 8:15 PM ET, NBC/Peacock. Schwarber's blast traveled 447 feet — the longest home run of the 2026 postseason so far.

facebook.long_form:
Kyle Schwarber stepped in and hit one 447 feet.

Bryce Harper, the very next batter, hit another one.

Back-to-back home runs in the eighth inning off Dylan Lee, and the Phillies — who were one out from facing a 2-0 series hole — had completely flipped the script. Then came the tenth inning: Alec Bohm launched a walk-off homer off Didier Fuentes, and Philadelphia had a stunning 4-3 extra-inning win that no Braves fan saw coming.

The series is tied 1-1. Tonight's winner-take-all Game 3 at Truist Park (8:15 PM ET, NBC/Peacock) is, suddenly, the most electric game on the 2026 postseason schedule.

This is why you watch October baseball. 🔔⚾

stories.title: Padres Sweep Cubs, Advance to NLDS to Face Brewers
stories.angle: San Diego Padres eliminated the Chicago Cubs 4-1 in Game 2 on September 30, completing a two-game Wild Card sweep. Gavin Sheets delivered a pinch-hit two-run homer. The Padres advance to the NLDS to face the Milwaukee Brewers. Cubs are eliminated.

facebook.long_form:
The San Diego Padres are headed to the NLDS, and the Chicago Cubs are headed home.

San Diego completed a two-game Wild Card sweep with a 4-1 victory at Petco Park on September 30. It was an efficient, professional performance — one in which Gavin Sheets provided the big moment with a pinch-hit two-run home run — but really, it felt like the Padres were in control from the start.

The Cubs had one of the best offensive lineups in the National League this year. But they managed just one hit against Dylan King in Game 1 and couldn't find their footing in Game 2, either.

San Diego advances to face the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLDS. If you weren't nervous about the Padres in October before, you might want to start now. 🔱

stories.title: White Sox Complete Historic Sweep of Astros — First Playoff Series Win Since 2005
stories.angle: Chicago White Sox swept the Houston Astros in the AL Wild Card Series, winning Game 2 on September 30. This is Chicago's first playoff series win since 2005. The White Sox — who had back-to-back 100+ loss seasons in 2023-24 — now advance to the ALDS. Colson Montgomery hit a 432-foot HR in Game 1. The turnaround story of the 2026 postseason.

x_posts.text:

facebook.long_form:
Stop and think about what just happened.

Two years ago, the Chicago White Sox lost 121 games — a modern MLB record for futility. They finished below .500 again in 2025. Then, in 2026, a team of young, unproven players scratched their way into the postseason for the first time in years.

And on September 30, they won a playoff series. Their first since 2005.

The White Sox swept the Houston Astros in the AL Wild Card round, finishing off the series with a victory that completed one of the most unlikely turnarounds in recent baseball history. GM Chris Getz. Manager Will Venable. Seven of nine starters under two years of MLB experience. And Colson Montgomery, who batted .099 in September, hitting a 432-foot home run in Game 1.

This team isn't just scrappy. They're believers. And now they're in the ALDS.

Get used to them. ⚾🖤

stories.title: Yankees Sweep Red Sox Without Judge — Aaron Judge Targets ALDS Return
stories.angle: New York Yankees swept the Red Sox in two games, winning Game 2 on September 30 by a score of 9-2. Ben Rice hit multiple home runs across the series. Aaron Judge was not on the Wild Card roster due to a right calf strain (soleus) but is targeting a return for the ALDS vs. Tampa Bay Rays. Yankees outscored Boston 18-2 across two games.

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Yankees outscored the Red Sox 18-2 without Aaron Judge.

Ben Rice: multiple home runs, including a grand slam. Cam Schlittler: 6.1 IP, 12 strikeouts in Game 1.

Judge is targeting the ALDS vs. Tampa Bay. Imagine what this lineup looks like healthy. ⚾ #Yankees

facebook.long_form:
The Yankees swept the Red Sox 2-0 — and they did it without Aaron Judge.

Ben Rice went yard multiple times, including a grand slam in Game 1. Cam Schlittler was unhittable in his Wild Card Game 1 start (6.1 IP, 12 strikeouts, no walks). New York outscored Boston 18-2 across the two games.

Judge, who has been nursing a moderate-grade right calf strain since September 16, was not on the Wild Card roster. He participated in batting practice and on-field running before the series, but the Yankees made the conservative call. With the ALDS vs. Tampa Bay ahead, the plan is to have him ready for a higher-stakes series.

If the Yankees are this good without the reigning AL MVP, what do they look like when he's back?

The Rays are about to find out. ⚾ #Yankees
facebook.image_caption: 18 runs. 2 allowed. No Aaron Judge. ⚾ The New York Yankees are through to the ALDS against the Rays — and Judge is targeting his return. #Yankees #RepBX

stories.title: Wild Card Round Wrap-Up — Three Sweeps and a Thriller, ALDS/NLDS Bracket Set
stories.angle: The 2026 Wild Card round produced three sweeps (Padres, White Sox, Yankees) and one dramatic series going to a Game 3 (Phillies-Braves tonight). ALDS: Yankees vs. Rays; White Sox vs. TBD in AL. NLDS: Padres vs. Brewers; Phillies/Braves winner vs. TBD.

2026 Wild Card results:
⚾ Padres sweep Cubs
⚾ White Sox sweep Astros
⚾ Yankees sweep Red Sox
⚾ Phillies vs. Braves → Game 3 TONIGHT

Three sweeps. One epic comeback. One final game to decide it all. The bracket is almost set. 🔥

facebook.long_form:
Let's recap the 2026 Wild Card round before the Division Series begins.

Three of the four series were sweeps. The Padres dismissed the Cubs efficiently. The White Sox shocked the Astros. The Yankees demolished the Red Sox. All three winning teams go into the ALDS/NLDS with momentum and healthy rosters.

Then there's the Phillies and the Braves — the one series that reminded us why we watch.

Down 0-1 after Atlanta's Game 1 win, Philadelphia punched back with one of the best postseason performances anyone's put together this October: back-to-back home runs in the eighth, a walk-off in the 10th, and a 4-3 comeback for the ages. Tonight, those teams play a winner-take-all Game 3 in Atlanta (8:15 PM ET, NBC/Peacock).

One game, everything on the line. That's baseball.
